pages.text: $(thing)Market Stalls$() stand in many villages, or build your own. Right-click one with an empty hand for today's prices and news; right-click with goods to sell the stack for coins (sneak to sell one).

Money comes in steps of nine: nine copper $(thing)pennies$() make a silver $(thing)shilling$(), nine shillings a gold $(thing)crown$(), and nine crowns a gold $(thing)sovereign$(). Craft nine coins into the next one up, or one into nine of the coin below. The market pays in the fewest coins it can.

Prices move with the seasons: grain is cheap after harvest and dear before the next, hay dearest at the end of winter, milk cheap in the spring flush. $(thing)Events$() push them further for a few days: a drought, a bumper harvest, a cloth fair, murrain among the herds, a hard winter.
Better produce pays more, from 60% for Poor up to 160% for Premium. Damp grain sells at a discount.

Now and then a $(thing)Travelling Farm Merchant$() in a straw hat comes by. He buys produce at the day's prices and sells seed of named cultivars, veterinary draughts, compost and tack, then moves on after two days.
